uniequip_002_blkkgt:
Among Degenbrecher's luggage is a case exclusively for storing her medals. After making exceedingly short work of her operator exam, the remaining downtime was spent with her enlightening our HR operators as to their significance.
- Knight-Champion of Kazimierz Medal
Black medal of crossed swordbreakers, lying unassumingly in center of case. Design makes it immediately clear that Kazimierz tailored this champion's medal to her. She reigned for three straight years and so was given three, but only the first was personally awarded to her by the Grand Knight after usurping the defender. Which is why she didn't throw it away, and why it's the one artifact of Kazimierz she still carries with her.
'Commemorative enough, barely.'
- 'Thanks'
Inverted triangle inscribed with Kjerag's holy Mount Karlan. Not issued by any official organization, rather forged for her by clan head Ratatos at the request of a household under Browntail rule. Degenbrecher had rescued said household's members from an avalanche.
'This first one was almost ten years ago now. I know they meant it nicely, and I don't mind how it looks. But the news spread, and now I get one of these medals from the Tri-Clans any time I do something similar. The cupboard at home is full of them.'
- 'The Silverashes' Sword and Shield'
Second medal from the left, sword and shield motif. All of Karlan Trade knows that those wearing this medal are free to act unimpeded wherever Karlan Trade is concerned. Initially a pass designed expressly for her by Enciodes, but as soon became apparent, nobody simply overlooks the presence of Degenbrecher. Its worth these days is instead in gently reminding others that she is affiliated with Karlan Trade.
'One day, I forgot to wear this one. Enciodes went that entire day quieter than usual, then in the end asked if I had any complaints with the company.'
- 'Kjeragandr's Soldier'
Third medal, honorary decoration issued by the Vine-Bead Court, was worn by Enya herself when she formally became the Saintess.
'This was the biggest protest the Saintess could make back then. I don't think much in particular about Kjeragandr—at most, I think I'd like to take Her on.'
- '10 Years'
To mark ten years of acquaintance, Enciodes rustled up a little gift for her, effectively commemorating her Karlan Trade decennial at the same time. It may not have been founded when they first met, but the blueprints were already laid out in his heart.
'I didn't even recall what it was commemorating when he gave me this. A token of thanks, I suppose, but I'm sure he just wanted to let me know that he still remembered the big words he said back when it all began. Speaking of Kjerag... if you're ever there as a tourist and want to find somewhere quiet, you can ask me.'
uniequip_003_blkkgt:
'You're late, Black Knight. That is a rare sight indeed.'
In the offices of Karlan Trade, the new President smiled at Degenbrecher as she came through the door, turning something over in his hand.
'I was told you had a new contract for me today, Gnosis.'
'I do. The papers are all on the desk. Although—' He paused. 'Did you see the new motorcycle parked downstairs?
'Karlan Trade has made a breakthrough in civil industry. We can finally manufacture motorcycles ourselves, and this one starts reliably at twenty below. No other nation has managed that.'
'Of course I saw it. It is hard to miss.'
Degenbrecher answered as she strolled toward the right side of the room, where a new display case stood—the new President's taste, no doubt.
Behind the glass sat a bearing split open by the cold. Degenbrecher remembered it: it had come out of the drill that broke down the first time they took mineral samples in Kjerag. After she had hauled a soot-smeared Enciodes out of the shaft, he had insisted on keeping the thing as a memento.
'If I remember rightly, there used to be a portrait of Enciodes hanging here.' Degenbrecher gestured toward the wall as she spoke to Gnosis.
'I took it down, Degenbrecher. If you received a work message from him in the middle of the night, and his face happened to be staring straight at you, what would you think?'
'So that was the reason... Thank you, Gnosis.'
'There is one more thing, in fact, and you will like it better.' Gnosis sounded uncharacteristically eager. 'We are putting together an ice fishing venture for tourists, and we developed a high-tech rod for it—it assists with the timing and force of the reel-in. I hear that you used to—'
'Gnosis.' Her voice was not raised, yet she made that one short name sound freezing cold.
'...My apologies. I must have been listening to rumors.'
'All you need to know is that it is in the past.'
The silence between them stretched on.
'As it happens, I had a gift prepared for you. Let it serve as an apology instead.' Gnosis left his seat and handed Degenbrecher the thing he had been holding all along.
Degenbrecher took it—a jet-black motorcycle key, stamped with the Karlan Trade emblem.
'It is better than the one you had, and we made a point of painting it in the red and black that suits you.' Gnosis smiled. 'I discussed it with Enciodes, and the staff agreed—
'It was decided unanimously. The very first motorcycle Karlan Trade ever built is yours.'
Degenbrecher's lips moved slightly, but in the end she said nothing—only pressed her thumb to the emblem and rubbed it once, lightly.
'Thank you.'
She turned and started for the door.
'Wait, Degenbrecher.' Gnosis's voice came from behind her. 'You still haven't signed the contract—'
'No need.'
Degenbrecher did not look back.
'I will be staying right here.' She slipped her right index finger through the key ring and raised it beside her ear.
'Until the day our roads run apart—' she said evenly, as though reciting a clause of a business agreement, '—I will ride away on this, and call it payment for all these years.'
Then the door swung open, and cold air poured into the office, stirring the papers on the desk.
Gnosis stood where he was and spoke quietly, his voice dissolving into the wind.
'Then, as you wish.'
